title: NTT Smile Energy says attackers breached its Eco Megane solar monitoring service and points were fraudulently exchanged
date_note: Publication date of Security NEXT; the company spotted the access on October 28 and its latest notice (3rd report) is dated 13 November.
summary: NTT Smile Energy says attackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain unauthorised access to its Eco Megane solar remote monitoring service, first detected on October 28. Smile e-Points were fraudulently exchanged in about 14,000 cases worth 8 million points, which it will compensate in full. Its 13 November notice says no trace of personal data leaking outside has been confirmed so far and solar generation and power sales were unaffected.
plain: Hackers broke into a Japanese solar monitoring service and misused customers' loyalty points; the company says it has found no sign so far that personal data left its systems.
exec: A software flaw let attackers into an energy-service provider's customer platform and misuse loyalty points; service is still being restored.
action: General advice: Eco Megane customers should change any password reused on other services and watch for phishing; operators should patch internet-facing web servers.
